answer: Split the economy's work through a prism into many distinct crafts, and pay each identity only for the marginal value its voyage adds in its chosen craft. An identity must forge a cumulative body of work in one craft over many epochs, reviewed by specialists in that craft alone. A farm can copy one successful voyage across a hundred clones, but copies add nothing new, so their combined pay barely exceeds one. To earn more, the operator must actually master many different crafts at once, a cost that grows with each clone instead of vanishing.
